name: Pool Corporation
headline: The largest pool-supply distributor, with a gross margin that held between 27% and 31% for 23 years.
what_it_does: Pool Corporation distributes pool chemicals, equipment and supplies to the contractors and stores that maintain, remodel and build pools. About 64% of sales are for maintenance and minor repair, 22% for remodels and upgrades and 14% for new construction. It serves about 5.5 million in-ground pools in the US.
why_it_passed: Its gross margin stayed between 27.3% and 31.3% every year from 2003 to 2025, through a housing collapse, a boom and an unwind.
Most of its sales depend on a large, slowly growing base of existing pools that need chemicals and replacement parts.
It earns high returns on its tangible capital through the cycle, and the working capital growth needs earns well.
Its operating margin (10% to 11%) sits well above SiteOne, the national landscape distributor (3.8% to 6.6%).
why_not_now: Here the price ($159.38) is below the analysis's central value range of $229.76 to $278.38, but it still falls short of the framework's bar. At that price the analysis expects about 8.3% a year, below the roughly 10% return it requires, so the analysis did not pass the price. A 30-year US Treasury bond pays 5.66%.
watch: Home Depot owns Heritage Pool Supply Group, the second national pool distributor; the analysis named this attack as the live threat to its margin and share.
Its chief executive left by mutual agreement in May 2026 after two years; the successor joined only in January 2026 from another company and is unproven.
It bought back shares in 2021 to 2025 at prices above its value, and holds $1.3 billion of debt.
